certificate.title: Claude Managed Terminal Agents for Month-End Close Completion

course.description: Run a full month-end close process from your terminal using Claude's Managed Agents. Drop your accounting files, run the .py file, and get bank reconciliation, trial balance review, adjusting JEs, variance analysis, and a CFO summary — all automated. Adapted from Mohamed Muse Said's LinkedIn post.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Claude Managed Terminal Agents for Month-End Close.

lessons.content:
Claude's Managed Agents let you run sandboxed AI employees directly from your terminal. For month-end close, the setup is minimal:

**Requirements:**
- Python installed on your machine
- Claude API access (with API key)
- A folder containing your accounting files

**What goes in the folder:**
- Bank statements (PDF or CSV)
- GL exports (CSV or Excel)
- Trial balance (current and prior period)
- Any supporting documents (sub-ledger details, schedules, prior workpapers)

**How it works:**
1. Place the `.py` file and your system prompt in a root folder
2. Drop your accounting files into the same folder
3. Run the script from your terminal
4. The agent processes everything end-to-end and saves each output as a separate report

The entire setup is just a `.py` file and a system prompt. No complex configuration, no server setup, no database.

*Source: [Mohamed Muse Said's LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:share:7469270301105750016)*
lessons.title: What You Need

lessons.content:
The agent starts by scanning your folder and identifying what's available:

**What the agent looks for:**
- Bank statements — identifies the bank, account, and statement period
- GL exports — maps account numbers and recognizes the chart of accounts structure
- Trial balances — confirms current vs. prior period and checks for balance
- Supporting documents — sub-ledger details, amortization schedules, fixed asset registers

**Why this matters:** The agent needs to understand what it's working with before it can run the close. This step ensures it doesn't try to reconcile a bank statement against the wrong GL account, or reference a document that doesn't exist.

**Output:** An inventory list of all documents found, with file type, period, and entity identified for each.
lessons.title: Step 1 — Document Identification

lessons.content:
The agent performs a full bank reconciliation:

**What it does:**
- Matches bank statement transactions to GL entries
- Flags **unmatched transactions** — items in the bank but not the GL, and vice versa
- Identifies **duplicates** — same amount, same date, potentially double-posted
- Surfaces **exceptions** — unusual amounts, out-of-period transactions, round-number entries

**Output:** A bank reconciliation report showing:
- Matched transactions (count and total)
- Unmatched items requiring investigation (with details)
- Duplicate flags
- Reconciling difference (should be zero if clean)

**What still needs you:** The agent flags issues but doesn't resolve them. Unmatched transactions need human judgment — is it a timing difference, a missing entry, or an error? The agent surfaces the question; you provide the answer.
lessons.title: Step 2 — Bank Reconciliation

lessons.content:
The agent reviews the trial balance for common issues:

**Checks performed:**
- **Balance check** — do debits equal credits? If not, flag the difference
- **Unusual account movements** — accounts with balances significantly different from prior period
- **Sign errors** — asset accounts with credit balances, liability accounts with debit balances
- **Dormant accounts** — accounts with zero activity that previously had balances
- **Rounding issues** — sub-cent differences that compound across accounts

**Output:** A trial balance review memo highlighting:
- Overall balance status (in balance / out of balance)
- List of accounts with unusual movements and the dollar change
- Any sign anomalies
- Accounts requiring follow-up

This step catches the issues that are easy to miss when you're deep in the close — the account that flipped signs, the prepaid that didn't amortize, the intercompany balance that's off by a journal entry.
lessons.title: Step 3 — Trial Balance Review

lessons.content:
Based on the bank rec and TB review, the agent drafts adjusting entries:

**Common AJEs the agent generates:**
- **Accruals** — expenses incurred but not yet recorded (utilities, services received)
- **Prepaids** — amortization of prepaid expenses based on schedules
- **Depreciation** — monthly depreciation based on fixed asset register
- **Deferred revenue** — recognition of revenue earned in the period
- **Reclassifications** — correcting misclassified transactions found during review

**Output format for each AJE:**
- Journal entry number
- Date
- Debit account(s) and amount(s)
- Credit account(s) and amount(s)
- Description/memo explaining the entry
- Supporting reference (which document or finding triggered this)

**Critical note:** These are *draft* entries. Every AJE needs human review before posting. The agent provides the analysis and drafts — you provide the approval. Never auto-post AI-generated journal entries without review.

*Source: [Mohamed Muse Said's LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:share:7469270301105750016)*
lessons.title: Step 4 — Draft Adjusting Journal Entries

lessons.content:
The agent compares current period to prior period and writes commentary:

**Analysis performed:**
- Period-over-period comparison for every account
- Calculation of dollar and percentage variances
- Identification of material movements (typically >10% or >$X threshold)
- Grouping of related variances (e.g., a revenue increase paired with corresponding COGS increase)

**Commentary generated:**
For each material variance, the agent writes a plain-English explanation:
- What changed
- Likely driver (based on transaction detail, if available)
- Whether the variance is expected or requires investigation
- Recommended follow-up action

**Output:** A variance analysis report with commentary, formatted for management review. This is typically the most time-consuming part of month-end close when done manually — the agent drafts it in minutes.

**What to review:** AI-generated commentary is based on pattern recognition, not business knowledge. Always validate the "why" — the agent may correctly identify that marketing spend increased 40% but incorrectly attribute it to a campaign when it was actually a vendor price increase.
lessons.title: Step 5 — Variance Analysis & Commentary

lessons.content:
The agent wraps up with two final deliverables:

**1. Month-End Close Checklist**
A status tracker showing every close task:
- Complete — bank rec done, TB reviewed, AJEs drafted
- Pending — items awaiting human input (unmatched transactions, AJE approvals)
- Requires Review — flags, anomalies, or items the agent couldn't resolve

This gives you a single view of where the close stands and what still needs your attention.

**2. One-Page CFO Summary**
An executive-ready document including:
- Key financial highlights for the period
- Material variances with brief explanations
- Risks or concerns identified during the close
- Recommended next steps
- Open items requiring management decision

**The full picture:** From a folder of raw accounting files to a complete close package — bank rec, TB review, draft AJEs, variance analysis, checklist, and CFO summary — all generated as separate reports by a single terminal command.

**To get the template and source code:** Comment "CLOSE" on Mohamed Muse Said's original LinkedIn post, or visit his Claude Accounting OS.

*Source: [Mohamed Muse Said's LinkedIn post](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:share:7469270301105750016)*
